info.description: [![Version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/pyngrok)](https://pypi.org/project/pyngrok) [![PyPI - Downloads](https://img.shields.io/pypi/dm/pyngrok)](https://pypistats.org/packages/pyngrok) [![Python Versions](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/pyngrok.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/pyngrok) [![Coverage](https://img.shields.io/codecov/c/github/alexdlaird/pyngrok)](https://codecov.io/gh/alexdlaird/pyngrok) [![Build](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/alexdlaird/pyngrok/build.yml)](https://github.com/alexdlaird/pyngrok/actions/workflows/build.yml) [![Code Quality](https://app.codacy.com/project/badge/Grade/b055cf6e3f1745098fab86a2923730b3)](https://app.codacy.com/gh/alexdlaird/pyngrok/dashboard?utm_source=gh&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=&utm_campaign=Badge_grade) [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/readthedocs/pyngrok)](https://pyngrok.readthedocs.io/en/stable) [![GitHub License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/alexdlaird/pyngrok)](https://github.com/alexdlaird/pyngrok/blob/main/LICENSE) `pyngrok` gives Python the complete [`ngrok` agent](https://ngrok.com/docs/gateway/agent), with programmatic tunnels for ingress, inspection, webhooks, demos, and APIs. [`ngrok`](https://ngrok.com) is a reverse proxy that opens secure tunnels from public URLs to localhost, and because `pyngrok` runs the real agent, you get everything it offers, from traffic policies and OAuth to its web inspector and request replay, all callable from Python. ## Installation `pyngrok` is available on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/pyngrok/) and can be installed using `pip`: ```sh pip install pyngrok ``` or `conda`: ```sh conda install -c conda-forge pyngrok ``` That's it! `pyngrok` is now available as a package to your Python projects, and `ngrok` is now available from the command line. ## Basic Usage ### Open a Tunnel To open a tunnel, use the [`connect`](https://pyngrok.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api.html#pyngrok.ngrok.connect) method, which returns a [`NgrokTunnel`](https://pyngrok.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api.html#pyngrok.ngrok.NgrokTunnel), and this returned object has a reference to the public URL generated by `ngrok` in its [`public_url`](https://pyngrok.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api.html#pyngrok.ngrok.NgrokTunnel.public_url) attribute. ```python from pyngrok import ngrok # Open a HTTP tunnel on the default port 80 # .ngrok.io" -> "http://localhost:80"> http_tunnel = ngrok.connect() # Open a SSH tunnel # "localhost:22"> ssh_tunnel = ngrok.connect("22", "tcp") # Open a named tunnel from the config file named_tunnel = ngrok.connect(name="my-config-file-tunnel") # Open an Internal Endpoint that's load balanced # "http://localhost:9000"> internal_endpoint = ngrok.connect(addr="9000", url="https://some-endpoint.internal", pooling_enabled=True) ``` The [`connect`](https://pyngrok.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api.html#pyngrok.ngrok.connect) method takes `kwargs` as well, which allows you to pass additional tunnel configurations that are supported by `ngrok` (or the `name` of a tunnel defined in `ngrok`'s config file), [as documented here](https://pyngrok.readthedocs.io/en/stable/#tunnel-configurations). > **Note:** `pyngrok` unifies `ngrok`'s "tunnel" (v2) and "endpoint" (v3) concepts behind a single API: `connect()` > returns an `NgrokTunnel` and handles the differences for you through the `config_version` you set. All `ngrok` > features are available to you through this. For v3-specific Endpoints, > see [Using v3 Endpoints](https://pyngrok.readthedocs.io/en/stable/#using-v3-endpoints). ### `ngrok`'s API The [`api`](https://pyngrok.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api.html#pyngrok.ngrok.api) method allows you to use the local `ngrok` agent to make requests against [the `ngrok` API](https://ngrok.com/docs/agent/cli-api/), if you have [set an API key](https://pyngrok.readthedocs.io/en/stable/#setting-the-authtoken-or-api-key). For example, here's how you would reserve a `ngrok` domain, then create a Cloud Endpoint with an associated traffic policy: ```python from pyngrok import ngrok domain = "some-domain.ngrok.dev" ngrok.api("reserved-domains", "create", "--domain", domain) ngrok.api("endpoints", "create", "--bindings", "public", "--url", f"https://{domain}", "--traffic-policy-file", "policy.yml") ``` ### Command Line Usage This package puts the default `ngrok` binary on your path, so all features of `ngrok` are available on the command line. ```sh ngrok http 80 ``` For details on how to fully leverage `ngrok` from the command line, see [`ngrok`'s official documentation](https://ngrok.com/docs/agent/cli/). ## Documentation For more advanced usage, `pyngrok`'s official documentation is available on [Read the Docs](https://pyngrok.readthedocs.io). ### Integration Examples - [Flask](https://pyngrok.readthedocs.io/en/stable/integrations.html#flask) - [Django](https://pyngrok.readthedocs.io/en/stable/integrations.html#django) - [MCP Servers](https://pyngrok.readthedocs.io/en/stable/mcp.html) - [Docker](https://pyngrok.readthedocs.io/en/stable/integrations.html#docker) - [Google Colab](https://pyngrok.readthedocs.io/en/stable/integrations.html#google-colaboratory) - [End-to-End Testing](https://pyngrok.readthedocs.io/en/stable/integrations.html#end-to-end-testing) ## Contributing If you would like to get involved, be sure to review the [Contribution Guide](https://github.com/alexdlaird/pyngrok/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst). Want to contribute financially? If you've found `pyngrok` useful, [sponsorship](https://github.com/sponsors/alexdlaird) would also be greatly appreciated!
